37616.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37616.question_text: Which of the following is not an external user of accounting information?
37616.explanation:
External users are people outside the business entity (organization) who use accounting information. Examples of external users are suppliers, banks, customers, investors, potential investors, and tax authorities.

The management are internal users of accounting information.

37617.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37617.explanation: Preparing a trial balance for a company serves to detect any mathematical errors that have occurred in the double-entry accounting system. If the total debits equal the total credits, the trial balance is considered to be balanced, and there should be no mathematical errors in the ledgers.

options.text: ascertain losses in a trading period
test arithmetical accuracy of ledger entries

37618.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37618.question_text: Which of the following is the reason why a seller allows a customer cash discount?
37618.explanation: Small cash discounts benefit the seller because they increase the likelihood that a buyer will pay quickly, therefore providing the seller with cash in a shorter period of time, as it is better to receive e.g. 95% of an invoice with a few days than wait 30 or more days to receive the full amount.

options.text: agreement to become a regular customer
introducing a new customer to the seller
settlement of account within a stated period

37619.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37619.explanation: A ledger is the principal book  that  contains a record of business transactions.

37621.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37621.question_text: Which of the following is not found in a trial balance?
37621.explanation: Closing stock is the leftover balance out of goods which were purchased during an accounting period. Total purchases are already included in the trial balance, Hence closing stock should not be included in the trial balance again. If it is included, the effect will be doubled.

37626.question_text: Where a wrong figure occurs in only one account with the second figure correctly stated, this is an error of
37626.explanation: A transposition error is a data entry error that occurs when two digits are accidentally reversed. It is where a bookkeeper accidentally reverses two adjacent digits, when recording transactional data.

37627.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37627.question_text: Which of the following is added to the proprietor's capital?
37627.explanation: Net profit is the actual profit after working expenses not included in the calculation of gross profit have been paid. That is, it is the profit after expenses have been deducted from gross profit. It makes up part of the business capital called plough-back profit

37646.question_text: In the preparation of bank reconciliation statement cheque are
37646.explanation:
Using the cash balance shown on the bank statement, add back any deposits in transit. Deduct any outstanding checks. This will provide the adjusted bank cash balance. Next, use the company's ending cash balance, add any interest earned and notes receivable amount.

All balances should be added to the bank statement

deduced from the the balance as per bank statement

37647.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37647.question_text: Which of the following is found in the general ledger?
37647.explanation: A sales account in the general ledger has a cumulative value or information regarding the actual sales ledger. By looking at this ledger, detailed information regarding the revenues can be obtained. It contains important information like date of sale, invoice number, name of the customer, amount of sale to name a few.

37652.question_text:

net profit = 0.1 x 12500 = 1250

gross profit = sales - cogs

net profit = gross profit - expenses

net profit = gross profit - expenses

37653.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37653.question_text: Which of the following is the equivalent of the receipts payment accounts?
37653.explanation:
Following are the characteristics of receipt and payment account:

  • It is a summary of the cash book.
  • We record all the cash receipts during the whole year on its debit side. ...
  • We include both receipts and payments in cash whether they are of capital and revenue nature.

From the above characteristics we can say the receipt and payments account is equivalent to the cash book which is used in recording all cash transactions

37658.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37658.question_text: Where records maintained are inadequate to facilitate the preparation of a trading and profit and loss accounts, this is described as
37658.explanation: Incomplete records refers to a situation in which an organization is not using double-entry bookkeeping. Instead, it is using a more informal accounting system, such as a single-entry system, to maintain a reduced amount of information about its financial results.

37659.explanation: The journal entry is a debit to the bad debt expense account and a credit to the accounts receivable account. (Remember your account receivables are credit sales that is the sales journal)

37660.explanation: It represents the total of all credit sales. Also known as trade debtors.

37677.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37677.question_text: The accounting principle that states that insignificant expenditures are not to be taken into account is the
37677.explanation: This accounting convention proposed that while accounting, only those transactions which have material impact on financial status of the organization will be considered  and other transactions which have insignificant effect will be ignored. It gives relative importance to an item or event.

37678.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37678.explanation: The realization principle is the concept that revenue can only be recognized once the underlying goods or services associated with the revenue have been delivered or rendered, respectively. Thus, revenue can only be recognized after it has been earned. Advance payment for goods .

37679.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37679.question_text: Where fixed capitals are maintained, partners' drawings are transferred to the
37679.explanation:
Asset accounts normally have debit balances, while liabilities and capital normally have credit balances. Income has a normal credit balance since it increases capital . On the other hand, expenses and withdrawals decrease capital, hence they normally have debit balances.

Therefore partners drawings would have a debit balance in the capital account

37696.explanation: General partner is a person who joins with at least one other person to form a business. A general partner has responsibility for the actions of the business, can legally bind the business and is personally liable for all the business's debts and obligations.

37713.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37713.question_text: A financial plan of action expressed in monetary terms is a/an
37713.explanation: A budget is an estimation of revenue and expenses over a specified future period of time.  Creating this spending plan allows you to determine in advance whether you will have enough money to do the things you need to do or would like to do. Budgeting is simply balancing your expenses with your income.

37714.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37714.question_text: Which of the following reserves is not used for bonus shares?
37714.explanation: capital redemption reserves fund is a part of a company's reserves and capital from money invested in shares that is not allowed to be given to shareholders in the form of dividends.

37715.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37715.question_text: When shares are sold 'at par' it means they are issued at
37715.explanation: When shares are issued at a price equal to their face value it is termed as shares issued at par. Par value is also known as nominal value or face value.

37717.question_text: Which of the following does not form part of shareholders fund?
37717.explanation: Debentures are a long-term security yielding a fixed rate of interest, issued by a company and secured against assets. It is a debt security issued by a company by a company to raise money. The holders are paid the amount lended with interest. They are not a source of equity financing

37723.explanation: The dual aspect concept states that every business transaction requires recordation in two different accounts.

37724.question_text: The amount for which a business is sold is that
37724.explanation: Consideration is a payment made by one party to another in exchange for the transfer of something of value. It must be of value to both parties entering into a transaction.

37725.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37725.question_text: Which of the following is a prime cost?
37725.explanation: Prime cost is the direct cost incurred during production. Royalty is paid on production basis and on sales basis. If it is paid on production basis then it is considered direct expense (prime cost) and debited to Trading Account
